column2: DialogueText
Hey Sheepherder! The sheep have gotten out of their pen!
Come down here and get them back in their pen!
Don't forget to close the gate when you're done!
You haven't gotten all the sheep in the pen!
Make sure you close the gate once they're inside!
Good job, you got them all back in their pen!
Meet me back up at the house,
I've got something to give to you.

This is my heron-marked blade.
You may need it in the times to come...
Please handle it with care.
Trollocs are attacking, protect the sheep!
Don't worry about me, protect the sheep!
I can't help you, I gave you my sword!
We have no chance against that thing!
Our only chance is to run!
I can't believe you beat that thing!
Thatching, thatching, always thatching. The Winespring Inn wants a tile roof, can you believe it?
Mark my words, lad, those Coplin boys will be trouble before Bel Tine.
Welcome to the Winespring Inn! Finest ale this side of the Mountains of Mist.
The spring up on the knoll never runs dry. Sweetest water in the Two Rivers.
Rand! Have you seen Nynaeve? She's looking for anyone who skipped their chores.
I'm going to see the world one day. Caemlyn, Tar Valon... all of it.
Psst. Want to see something? I found a badger down by the Old Road.
Don't tell Nynaeve. She'd have my hide with that switch of hers.
Halt! State your business in the Inner City.
...Very well. Mind the Queen's Guards, and keep off the palace steps.
The Queen's Blessing has the best room in the New City, if you ask me.
Trouble in the streets lately. Red cloths, white cloths... stay out of it.
Mother says a Daughter-Heir should not talk to strangers in the gardens.
But you look like you have seen more of the world than I have. Tell me of it sometime.
I do be a river man, not a city man. Caemlyn be too far from the water.
If you ever need passage down the Erinin, look for the Spray in Whitebridge.
A gleeman's tales are worth a coin or two, young friend.
Did you know the topless towers of Cairhien were never finished? Now there is a story.
Daes Dae'mar, the Game of Houses. Every word you say here has three meanings.
Choose your friends in Cairhien carefully, outlander. Choose your enemies more carefully still.
Spare a coin? The Foregate burned and the nobles never noticed.
They say the King hoards grain in the Sun Palace. I say the towers are hollow.
The grid of the city was laid out by Ogier masons. Every street exactly so.
Please do not walk on the grass. It was imported from Andor at great expense.
The topless towers have stood half-built since the Aiel War.
Climb the ladders if you like. Mind the drop.
The Stone of Tear has never fallen. Not once in three thousand years.
Keep your hands where I can see them, outlander.
The Erinin brings the grain and the Erinin takes the coin.
Watch your step on the piers, the planks are rotten and the river is deep.
Fresh eels! Caught this morning below the Stone.
No channeling in Tear, mind. The Defenders do not take kindly to it.
The Maule stinks of fish and the High Lords stink of politics.
If you have a strong arm, there is always work with the Defenders.
Novices are not supposed to talk to visitors. Please do not tell the Mistress of Novices.
The Tower has a hundred levels and I have scrubbed every one of them.
The Tower grounds are closed to the public. Admire it from the steps.
An Aes Sedai is not to be disturbed. Move along.
Ogier built this city, you know. Every bridge, every street. Hasty work, only three hundred years.
I would very much like to see a stedding again. The trees here are so young.
Four bridges in and four bridges out, and a toll on every one of them.
Silk from Arafel, ice peppers from Shienar. Have a look, friend.
Peace favor your sword, traveler. Fal Dara is the last light before the Blight.
The keep has stood against Trollocs for a thousand years. It will stand tonight.
Every Shienaran man carries a sword. Every woman knows how to use one.
The Gap is quiet. Too quiet. Keep your lantern lit.
Good steel comes from the forges here, hammered in the cold.
Snow in the streets till Sunday. Mind the ice on the keep stairs.
Bloody flaming Trollocs took my goat last winter.
If you see a goat with one horn, that one's mine.
The Panarch's Palace is closed. The Panarch's Palace is always closed.
Tanchico has three hills and three kinds of trouble. Pick one.
Silk, dyes, honey from the Mountains of Mist! Best prices in the Souk.
Mind the stairs down to the harbour. The steps are older than the city.
Ships from Illian, ships from the Sea Folk, ships from places with no names.
The Great Dome? The Panarch's folk say it is older than the Breaking.
Race you to the top of the medina! Last one up is a Whitecloak.
I know a secret way down the cliff. It's a ladder. Don't tell.
The Council of Nine do say the King rules Illian. The King do say otherwise.
Mind the canals after dark. The water be deeper than it looks.
A boat ride through the canals, two coppers. Bridges be free.
The reeds grow thick this year. Good for baskets, bad for boats.
I have sworn the oath of the Hunters of the Horn. Have you heard it sounded?
Every road out of Illian leads to the Horn of Valere. I just do not know which.
Flowers for your lady? The ones from the marsh never wilt.
The Bees of Illian, they call us. Busy, busy, and the honey all goes to the Nine.
Treasure... there is treasure here, friend. Take what you like.
No one leaves Shadar Logoth with more than they brought. Except me.
The Wayfarer's Rest, best inn on the Arinelle. Mind the stairs, the cellar floods.
The White Bridge? Older than the town. Harder than steel. Nobody knows who built it.
Nobody takes the ferry since the bridge. Cheaper to walk.
The water runs cold and fast below the bridge. I have fished men out of it.
Did you know the bridge looks like glass but you can't see through it?
Thom the gleeman said he'd teach me to juggle. Then he left.
The Stag and Lion welcomes you. Rooms upstairs, stew downstairs, and no fighting.
The Whitecloaks have been asking questions. I did not tell them anything.
Baerlon is a mining town, whatever the fine folk say. Iron and silver.
The hills north of here are full of old shafts. Mind where you step.
Walk in the Light, friend. The Children watch over Baerlon.
Darkfriends hide in plain sight. Report anything unusual to the Children.
You came all this way with no cloak? You will catch your death.
When we get home, there will be words. Many words.
Master Luhhan has me at the forge till dark. The whole village wants new hinges before winter.
The hills up toward the Mountains of Mist are full of wolves this year. Keep to the road.
I see things around people. Sparks, and a shadow. Don't ask.
The stable boy has a hole in his boot. See? Sometimes it's just boots.
Barges from Baerlon, barges to Caemlyn. Everything on the Arinelle stops at Whitebridge.
Down those stairs is the quay. Mind the crates, the cooper will have your ears.
The Children do not enter this cursed place. Nor should you.
Shadows move in the ravines after dark. Do not follow them.
I can smell violence, you know. Old killings. The mountains north of here reek of it.
The camp outside the walls is for traders. Nobody sleeps outside the walls by choice.
Low Caemlyn, they call it. Outside the walls, outside the law.
The Queen's Guards never come this far. Neither does the Queen's bread.
Lost? Everyone gets lost in the alleys. Two coppers and I'll show you the way.
Don't go in the Inner City. They make you wash.
Welcome to the Foregate! Gleemen, jugglers, and the best fried bread outside Andor.
The nobles inside the walls think we are rabble. We think they are boring.
The Alguenya carries grain south to the Erinin and gossip north to the Tower.
Mind the quay stairs. The river is higher than it looks.
The Maule floods every spring. We put the chickens on the roof.
Up on the hill the High Lords have gardens. Down here we have mud.
The old quarter, dear. Houses leaning on houses, and every roof a different colour.
An Aes Sedai ordered a shawl with a blue fringe. I have not slept in three days.
That mountain is Dragonmount. Folk say it still smokes some nights.
Nobody farms on its slopes. Nobody sensible, anyway.
Blue from the Sea Folk, red from the hills. My hands have not been clean in twenty years.
The alleys up here were never planned. Every house just leans on the next.
The Sea of Storms do bring the ships and the ships do bring the coin.
Fish, olives, and lacquerware. Nothing leaves this harbour without a tally.
The Perfumed Quarter, dear. It do not smell of perfume. It never did.
Every alley here ends at a canal. Learn to swim or learn to ask directions.
